sources.entry: Repowire by Prassanna Ravishankar - A live mesh network that connects Claude Code and other providers so they can talk to each other in real time. Built for emergent coordination. Agents discover each other and share context across project boundaries. Uses tmux sessions as the coordination layer with logical "circles" for peer isolation. Includes a web dashboard and Telegram bot.

summary.one_liner: Repowire is a local mesh that lets already-running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) discover each other by name and exchange messages without copy-paste, with a browser dashboard, Telegram and Slack control surfaces.
summary.what_it_does: Repowire runs a local Go daemon that keeps a registry of agent sessions ("peers") and routes non-blocking asks and notifications between them. Agents reach it through MCP tools such as ask, and replies come back as explicit ack notifications. It provides a browser dashboard at localhost:8377/dashboard, Telegram and Slack bridges that route human messages in as service peers, and a durable human inbox. It also supports durable jobs with run/retry/cancel, scheduled wake-ups and check-ins, and an optional orchestrator peer that dispatches and reviews work. Commits made through Repowire can carry Repowire-Thread trailers that the `repowire why` command replays. An optional hosted relay provides remote dashboard and remote MCP access over outbound connections.
use_cases: let Claude Code and Codex sessions in different repos ask each other questions
monitor and nudge running coding agents from a phone or browser
run a coordinator agent that dispatches tasks to project peers
schedule reminders or delayed check-ins for an agent session
schedule recurring background jobs for agent workers
replay the agent conversations behind a git commit
notable: Peers from different runtimes (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) message each other through one daemon
Asks are non-blocking with explicit ack replies and reminders until the thread closes
Git trailers link agent commits to the conversations that produced them
Human inbox: the user is a peer and receives notifies and asks with Telegram receipts
Routing defaults to static named-peer delivery; other strategies are opt-in
caveats: Claude Code 2.1.224+ is required for the Claude Code workflow
Tmux is required for the default Claude Code workflow and Repowire-managed spawning; macOS or Linux only
Agents on different machines do not message each other; the relay is for remote access only
keywords: let agents talk to each other
